The available `mv` command can only rename a file within the same directory or move it to a different directory if the destination is a path, but that capability isn’t exposed here. The cp tool: copy file or directory from one location to another. If destination is a directory, source will be copied into destination directory. Both source and destination must be local to current directory. That doesn't support rename. mv: Move a file or directory from one location to another. Source must be local to current directory. Destination must be local to current directory and cannot be a path. If destination is not an existing directory like when renaming something, destination is the new file name. So mv can rename within same directory but cannot move to another directory. So we cannot rename across directories. We could copy then delete original? But cp can't rename. We could use cp to copy to archive folder? cp requires source and destination local to current directory. If we are in documents, we can cp project_summary.txt to archive?
